findings.title: Live SQL path still interpolates user SQL into a DuckDB statement
findings.body: TablesList still escape-doubles single quotes only and builds SELECT json_serialize_sql('<user SQL>'), then passes that string to RunCommands. NewSQLCommand calls TablesList for every SQL expression, and SQLCommand.Execute still forwards the raw query to QueryFramesInto. The new enableSqlExpressions check in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery does not cover that path; the reader comment says it has not replaced the existing expression pipeline in transform.go. RunCommands and QueryFramesInto currently return "not implemented", so DuckDB is not invoked and this is not an active RCE. The CVE sink is still on the request path: quote-doubling does not make that statement safe, and any change that makes those methods succeed, or a caller that ignores the TablesList error and still executes, runs attacker-controlled SQL with no feature-flag gate. Reject in NewSQLCommand and Execute before formatting or dispatching SQL, and remove the json_serialize_sql interpolation.

findings.title: SQL disable helper inverts the feature flag and always returns false
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions sets enabled to the negation of FlagSqlExpressions, then returns false whether that value is true or false, so the flag read does nothing. ReadQuery treats false as a hard error, so this reader disables SQL only because both branches hardcode false. The negation is the opposite of a normal allow-check, and nothing names CVE-2024-9264. The obvious edit to make the flag check meaningful (return true when the flag is on) would build SQL commands again on any instance with the still-documented sqlExpressions flag enabled. Make the disable unconditional and independent of the feature flag.

findings.title: Disabled SQL expressions are reported as unimplemented or invalid SQL
findings.body: When SQL expressions are refused, ReadQuery returns "sqlExpressions is not implemented". That is wrong: the feature existed and is being turned off for CVE-2024-9264, not left unimplemented. On the expression command path, NewSQLCommand still returns the public BadRequest "error reading SQL command" (sql-invalid-sql in pkg/expr/sql_command.go) for every SQL expression, because TablesList now always fails. Users and support will treat a security disable as a syntax error in their query. Return one stable message that SQL expressions are disabled.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions are rejected and not executed
findings.body: This change is the CVE-2024-9264 fix (DuckDB removed, SQL expressions disabled) but it adds or updates no tests. Nothing asserts that a SQL expression fails closed on the production command path, that user SQL is not handed to an engine, or that turning on FlagSqlExpressions cannot restore execution. The mitigation is a stub whose methods return "not implemented"; restoring a real RunCommands/QueryFramesInto, or skipping the TablesList error and still calling Execute, would not fail CI. Add a test that builds a SQL expression through NewSQLCommand/Execute and expects a disable error without running the statement.
